facts.statement: The genus Shaochilong contains only one species, Shaochilong maortuensis.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Shaochilong maortuensis

facts.statement: Specimens of Shaochilong were discovered in Inner Mongolia and were originally described by Hu in 1964 as a species of Chilantaisaurus.
facts.quote: All of these specimens were discovered in Inner Mongolia and described by Hu in 1964 as a species of Chilantaisaurus

facts.statement: The genus was informally named "Alashansaurus" by Chure in 2000.
facts.quote: The genus was informally named "Alashansaurus" by Chure in 2000

facts.statement: A 2009 re-description by Brusatte and colleagues identified Shaochilong as a carcharodontosaurid, marking the first such dinosaur recognized from Asia.
facts.quote: a re-description by Brusatte and colleagues in 2009 found that it was a carcharodontosaurid, the first recognized from Asia

facts.statement: Shaochilong lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago during the Aptian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Shaochilong is estimated to have been 5 to 6 meters long based on the length of its maxillary tooth row.
facts.quote: Shaochilong length – based on the length of the maxillary tooth row – is estimated at 5 to 6 m

facts.statement: With an estimated femur length of 61.5 cm, Shaochilong likely weighed approximately 500 kg.
facts.quote: Estimated length of the femur is 61.5 cm which suggests the whole animal weighed approximately 500 kg

facts.statement: Due to its small size, Shaochilong likely occupied a unique ecological niche compared to other carcharodontosaurids.
facts.quote: In combination with its comparatively small size, it could have had a unique ecological role in comparison to other members of this family

facts.statement: Shaochilong appears more closely related to Gondwanan carcharodontosaurians like Carcharodontosaurus and Giganotosaurus than to Laurasian ones.
facts.quote: Shaochilong appears to be more closely related to the Gondwanan carcharodontosaurians (Tyrannotitan, Carcharodontosaurus, Mapusaurus, Giganotosaurus) than the Laurasian ones

facts.statement: Recent research has questioned whether Shaochilong belongs to the carcharodontosaurid family.
facts.quote: However, some more recent research has questioned this taxon's position as a carcharodontosaurid

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses have recovered Shaochilong as a member of Tyrannosauroidea rather than Carcharodontosauridae.
facts.quote: In the description of the metriacanthosaurid Alpkarakush, Shaochilong was recovered as a member of Tyrannosauroidea in the phylogenetic analyses of tetanurans

facts.statement: Analyses associated with the description of Tameryraptor recovered Shaochilong as a tyrannosauroid based on shared autapomorphies.
facts.quote: In the description of the large African carcharodontosaurid Tameryraptor, all analyses recovered Shaochilong as a tyrannosauroid as it shares several autapomorphies with the grouping

facts.statement: The describers of Yuanmouraptor have placed Shaochilong back into the Carcharodontosauridae family.
facts.quote: The describers of the metriacanthosaurid Yuanmouraptor have placed Shaochilong back to Carcharodontosauridae again

facts.statement: Shaochilong fossils were found in the Miaogou Formation at the Maortu locality, though they were originally interpreted as coming from the nearby Ulansuhai Formation.
facts.quote: The material referred to Shaochilong, IVPP V.2885.1-7, was found in the Miaogou Formation (Maortu locality; originally interpreted as the nearby Ulansuhai Formation)

facts.statement: A lectotype was established in 2010 to address the possibility that the Shaochilong specimens originated from multiple individuals.
